title: Non-Additive Compile-Time Features (Mutually Exclusive Features)
damaged_code:
```toml
# Cargo.toml of dependency 'crypt_lib'
[features]
# Non-additive feature definition: enabling both causes compilation failure
use_openssl = []
use_rustls = []
```
pattern: Configuring build or compilation flags in a package manager that are non-additive, remove functionality, or override existing type signatures when enabled.
why_bad: If dependency C features are mutually exclusive, a downstream crate that depends on both crate A (requiring feature `use_openssl`) and crate B (requiring feature `use_rustls`) will fail to resolve dependencies and fail compilation. It breaks the unified cargo compile model.
detection: Cargo features or build configurations that trigger compilation errors if toggled simultaneously, or conditional compilation targets that modify public function signatures.
fix: Refactor package flags to be strictly additive; preserve all type definitions and signatures across features, implementing stubs or runtime toggles instead.
source: Jon Gjengset - *Rust For Rustaceans_ Idiomatic Programming for Experienced Developers* (2021, No Starch Press).pdf, Chapter 6.
